coordinates.note: Campus-grade: the Nominatim/OpenStreetMap point for the plant outline. DANSS sits in a room under reactor unit 4 (its distance to the core is 10.7-12.7 m); no fetched source gives the hall coordinate, so the position is known only to about the size of the plant (~1.5 km).

depth_mwe.quote: The reactor building provides about 50~m water-equivalent shielding against the cosmic background.

name: Kalinin Nuclear Power Plant reactor building (DANSS)

summary.plain: A room inside the reactor building of the Kalinin nuclear power plant in Russia, a few metres below a power reactor, where the DANSS detector sits on a movable platform.
summary.technical: Room below the core of a VVER-1000 reactor at the Kalinin NPP, 350 km NW of Moscow; the reactor building supplies about 50 m.w.e. of cosmic-ray shielding. Marked with a campus-grade point.
